answer: Agents selling sable sketches of a glacier must not forge extra trusted identities by copying their reputation during key rotation. Store each reputation history under one permanent record ID. A migration signed by the old key atomically replaces its authorized key, and buyers check the current registry before trusting any score. Multiple aliases pointing to that record share its contract limit; they never receive separate limits. This prevents reputation cloning through migrations, but does not stop an operator earning several independent records or selling control of one.
